In the present appeal filed under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the appellant-convict has prayed for suspension of sentence imposed by the concerned Trial Court during the pendency of the appeal.

2. The present appellant was tried before the concerned Trial Court alongwith accused Bhushan Kumar and the Trial Court, i.e., Special Judge (POCSO), Patna vide order dated 15.07.2022 convicted the present appellant for the offences punishable under Sections 376(D) read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and the appellant was sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.50,000/- Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.641 of 2022(10) dt.18-08-2023 and in default of payment of fine, to further undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for six months

. The appellant was further sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for five years for the offence punishable under Section 365 of the Indian Penal Code and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine to further undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for three months.

The appellant was also sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for two years for the offence Sujit Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167741041/
1 punishable under Section 506 of the Indian Penal Code and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to further undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for three months.

sentences.text:
3. Heard Mr. Dhirendra Kumar Sinha, learned Advocate for the appellant assisted by Mr. Ajay Kumar Sinha, Km. Shashi Bala Verma, learned APP for the respondent-State and Mr. Lalan Kumar appearing on behalf of original first informant.
4.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellant has mainly contended that even as per the case of the prosecution, the present appellant alongwith co-accused Rajesh Kumar and Bhushan Kumar came on a red colour motorcycle and they forcibly made the victim/informant sit on the bike between Rajesh Kumar and Bhushan Kumar and the victim was taken Patna High Court CR. APP (DB)
No.641 of 2022(10) dt.18-08-2023 away by the concerned accused persons on 20.04.2020 at about 06:00 p.m.

It is further submitted that the victim, who has been examined as PW3 before the Trial Court, has specifically stated in her examination-in-chief that after she was kidnapped by the three accused persons, they came at village Bhajaur and thereafter the other two co-accused, Rajesh Kumar and Bhushan Kumar had taken away the victim from the said village and they went to village Chananpur of Masaurhi Police Station and at the said place, i.e. in village Chananpur, the other two co
- accused, namely, Rajesh Kumar and Bhushan Kumar committed rape on her during night hours.

5. At this stage, learned counsel for the appellant has referred to the findings recorded by the Trial Court on the basis of the evidence produced before the said Court that the present appellant has not participated in the offence of rape.

However, the Trial Court has observed that the present appellant was having common intention and, therefore, in furtherance of the common intention of all, the incident in question took place and, therefore, the appellant has been convicted under Section 376(D) read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

It is further pointed out from the record, i.e.,
from paragraph 36 of the impugned judgment and order of conviction that the Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.641 of 2022(10) dt.18-08-2023 appellant has been acquitted for the offence punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
Learned Advocate, therefore, urged that the present appellant be released on bail by suspending sentence imposed by the Trial Court during pendency of the appeal.

6. It is further submitted that even assuming, without admitting, that the appellant was present at the place of occurrence when the victim was kidnapped, the Trial Court has convicted the present appellant for the offence punishable under Section 365 of the Indian Penal Code and he was sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for five years.
It is pointed out from the records that the appellant is in jail since 23.04.2020, i.e., since last more than three years and he may be enlarged on bail.
7. On the other hand, learned APP appearing for the respondent-State has vehemently opposed the request made by the appellant.
Learned APP has referred to the deposition given by the victim (PW3).

It is submitted that specific allegations are levelled against the present appellant that the appellant alongwith two other accused had kidnapped the victim and thereafter the two other co-accused took the victim to another village and committed the offence of rape.

It is further submitted Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.641 of 2022(10) dt.18-08-2023 that no error is Sujit Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167741041/
2 committed by the Trial Court while convicting the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 376(D) read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: Learned APP has also referred to the deposition of the other prosecution witnesses and the medical evidence.

Learned APP, therefore,
urged that when the Trial Court has sentenced the present appellant for a period of 20 years, this Court may not release the appellant on bail.

8. Mr. Lalan Kumar, learned Advocate appearing for the first informant, has also supported the submissions canvassed by learned APP and urged that the request made by the appellant may not be entertained at this stage.

9. We have considered the submissions canvassed by learned counsel for the parties and we have also perused the materials placed on record and the deposition upon which the reliance is placed by learned counsel appearing for the parties.
It is pertinent to note that even as per the case of the prosecution, the appellant was not present when the two other co-accused committed the offence of rape.

Even the victim has specifically stated that two other accused, namely, Rajesh Kumar and Bhushan Kumar have committed the offence of rape during night hours by giving threats to victim at village Chananpur.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.641 of 2022(10) dt.18-08-2023
Even the Trial Court has also observed in paragraph-35 that the present appellant did not directly participate in the offence of rape.
However, he has been convicted for the said offence read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
It is pertinent to note that the appellant has been acquitted for the offence punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.

10. From the evidence produced before us, at the most, it can be said that the appellant was present alongwith the two other co-accused when the victim was kidnapped from village Bhajaur and for the said act, the present appellant has been convicted under Section 365 of the Indian Penal Code and he was sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of five years.

It is not in dispute that appellant is in jail since 23.04.2020.
11.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the present case, we are inclined to consider the request made by the appellant for grant of bail.

12. Accordingly, the appellant above named, is ordered to be released on bail, during pendency of the appeal, on his executing a personal bond of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand) with two sureties of like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VII-cum- Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.641 of 2022(10) dt.18-08-2023 Special Judge, POCSO, Patna in connection with Special Case (POCSO) No.80/2020, arising out of Bhagwanganj P.S. Case No.55 of 2020 and sentence imposed by concerned Trial Court is suspended till final disposal of the present appeal.
13. Realization of fine is stayed till final disposal of the appeal.

(Vipul M. Pancholi, J.) ( Chandra Shekhar Jha, J.) Sanjay/-
